analysis.title: USA: Consumer Confidence Well Above Expectations; New Home Sales Decline Less Than Expected
key_insights: The Conference Board consumer confidence index rose 7.5pt to 91.7 in October from an upwardly revised 84.2 in September, well above the GS and median forecast of 81.0. It is now in line with levels from the beginning of the year.
Both components rose from upwardly revised September levels: the present situation index gained 8.6pt to 120.4 and the expectations index gained 6.9pt to 72.6.

The labor differential (share saying jobs are plentiful minus share saying jobs are hard to get) rose 2.4pp to 5.3%. Jobs plentiful rose 2.4pp to 26.7% and jobs hard to get was flat at 21.4%. This reverses most of last month's large decline.
Median 12-month ahead inflation expectations fell 0.4pp to 4.7%, still 0.2pp above the February level, just before the start of the war.

In write-in responses, references to prices, the high cost of food and groceries, and oil and diesel prices continued to rise. Comments about war/conflict eased for a second straight month but remained elevated. The cutoff date for preliminary results was October 21.

New home sales fell 0.6% to a 676k SAAR in September, a smaller decline than the GS forecast of -4.8% (651k) and the median forecast of -4.5% (651k). August was revised down 4k to 680k SAAR, a +5.1% gain.

By region, September new home sales fell in the South (-6.6%) and Midwest (-7.3%), partly retracing the largest one-month percent increase in the series' history in August. They rose in the Northeast (+28.0%) and West (+21.4%).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Printed far above the 81.0 GS and median forecast and above the prior revised 84.2. Both the present situation and expectations components rose, and the level is back to where it stood at the start of the year.
